done.why: I'd just gotten the platinum bar and was heading east out of the Loud Room when the world told me I'd used all 30 turns it allows. I was still going; I wasn't bored yet.

about: Zork, but not quite the Zork I half-remember. A white house with a boarded door, a trap door under the rug, and a cellar full of things that want to kill you or rob you. You grab a lantern and a glowing sword, cut a troll's head off, get sized up by a thief, and start collecting treasure. The changes are in the map: passages that should go somewhere end in black water, and the Round Room has cave-ins blocking most of its exits.

moments.note: The trap door slams shut and someone bars it behind me. Then the sword starts glowing. Nicely ominous.
Troll fight ends with his head coming off and a black fog eating the body. The 'axe to grind' line the turn before made me grin.
The chasm path northeast runs straight into cold black water with no far side. Then a thief is just leaning on the wall. Didn't expect the map to be cut off like that.
Southwest from the chasm dumped me right back in the East-West Passage. So the chasm is a dead end both ways? Felt like a loop.
'Bar bar ...' - the room echoes and eats my command. Annoying for about one turn.
Guessed 'echo' and the acoustics changed. Felt clever for a second, and the bar came up next turn.

wished: Find out what's east of the Loud Room, or up its stairs, before the session ended.
Learn what the black water is for - swim it, or find a boat, or anything other than walking back with wet feet.
Chase the thief or at least follow where he went; he just left and nothing came of it.
Know which Round Room exits are actually open without having to bump into each cave-in one at a time.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: First moment the place felt hostile instead of just old. Committed me to going forward.

lines.line: He appears to have an axe to grind with you.
lines.why: Dumb pun in the middle of a fight. Exactly the tone I wanted.

lines.line: the path runs down into water, black and still and very cold, and your light finds no other side to it.
lines.why: The one line that told me this was a changed map and not the one in my head. Good image too.
The world mocking my command. Irritating and funny in equal measure, and it pushed me to try 'echo'.

fun.why: Short and punchy. A fight I won, a treasure I had to think about for a second, and two surprises in the map. Never had a dull stretch in 30 turns.

engagement.why: I wanted to keep going when it stopped me. The barred trap door and the glowing sword kept me pushing forward rather than wandering.

difficulty.why: Nothing stopped me for more than a turn. The troll fell in five swings, the thief wandered off on his own, and the Loud Room cost me one guess. The only friction was the chasm loop and not knowing which Round Room exits were blocked.

interestingness.why: Mostly it's the Zork I expected, which is fine but not new. The black water and the cave-ins are the hooks that made it feel different, and I only touched them.

prose.why: Terse where it should be and flavored where it counts. The water description at 23 and the troll fight lines were the best; room descriptions are plain functional.
